newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cypriot president urges calm as police patrol.
newsitem.headline: Cypriot president urges calm as police patrol.

text.p: Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides urged calm among Greek Cypriots planning protests on Friday's anniversary of the declaration of the Turkish-Cypriot breakaway state in northern Cyprus.
Greek Cypriot police in riot gear were out in force near the U.N.-patrolled "Green Line" dividing the capital Nicosia, erecting barbed wire across approach roads.
Two Greek Cypriots were killed in August by Turks while demonstrating in the island's buffer-zone against Turkish occupation of northern Cyprus.

"Many times in the past the Greek Cypriot people have paid dearly for the mistaken action of organised groups or individuals who did not have the responsibility for the handling of our national problem," Clerides said in a national address.

"As the Greek Cypriot people can no longer afford such experiments and adventures the government is determined not to allow anybody, through irresponsible actions, to jeopardise its own responsible handlings," he said.

Students and refugee organisations are planning a mass rally in Nicosia on Friday morning to condemn the 13th anniversary of the creation of the Turkish Cypriot breakaway state, which is recognised only by Ankara.
Students are given time out of class by state schools to attend the protests.
Turkey invaded northern Cyprus in 1974 following a coup in Nicosia engineered by the military junta ruling Greece.
